newsitem.title: INDIA: India Kinetic sees new motorcycle boosting exports.
newsitem.headline: India Kinetic sees new motorcycle boosting exports.

text.p: Indian two-wheeler maker Kinetic Engineering Ltd will export its K4 motorcycle, launched in February, to south Asian markets as soon as the vehicle has proved itself domestically, a company official said.
"The K4-100 has a very very big export market," Kinetic chairman Arun Firodia, told Reuters in an interview at his headquarters in the western city of Pune.
"We have decided first to launch and establish it in India. After that there is plenty of export potential. We could export at least 3,000 to 4,000 per month."

Indian sales of two-wheelers, the segment Firodia plans to tap, are driven by demand from the estimated 84 million middle- and lower-middle class people with incomes ranging between 20,000 and 62,000 rupees annually.

Firodia said the K4-100, a medium-range motorcycle, which was launched in Pune in February this year would be made available to dealers all over the western state of Maharashtra by the end of next month.
"This month we are opening other centres for the K4-100 in one half of Maharashtra," Firodia said last week. "The rest will be opened next month."

The K4-100 will face competition from Marvel, a 100-cc. scooter manufactured by Kinetic Honda Motor Co the local unit of Japan's Honda Motor Corp, which has sold 2,500 units since deliveries began in June.
Firodia said 2,000 units of the K4-100 had been sold since its launch. He believed it would fill the gaps in his firm's export strategy.

"Right now we are unable to export to Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam because these countries require K4-type vehicles. The type of vehicle we (used to) make they don't require," Firodia said.
"When we make K4-100 (for export) we'd like to export it starting from Sri Lanka all the way to the Philippines."
The K4-100 is powered by an indigenously developed 92-cc. four-stroke engine, with a dual steel tubular chassis and 65 km per litre fuel efficiency.
"It's a step-through. It has some of the characteristics of a motorbike. It offers the power and performance of a motorcycle and the comfort and convenience of a scooter."
He expected to sell 4,000 units of the K4 by the end of the year, with demand growing over the next few years.

"Customer response has been very positive," Firodia added. "Reports in the press say it has the best fuel consumption of any vehicle in the world. By the year 2000, we would expect to be selling 100,000 units per annum."
The K4-100, which meets stricter emission standards due to take effect from 2000, will give Kinetic a march over its competitors, officials said.

"Actually we have an advantage because it will be absolutely ready for fuel emission norms by 2000 plus it will be the best fuel-efficient, plus as Kinetic policy we have kept the price as low as possible," assistant general manager A.V. Chitale said.
"There is no other vehicle available with these characteristics at this price," he added.
Firodia said Kinetic also had plans to establish a presence at the high-powered-end end of the two-wheeler segment, and would start work on a 150-cc motorcycle very soon.
"The 150 cc motorcycle will be double the cost of the K4-100," he said. "It's certainly targeted at the upper end. We hope to introduce it within the next two years."
Last year Kinetic exported 10,000 vehicles, the bulk constituted of its Luna and Pride low-power two-wheelers.
Kinetic has a 27 percent share of India's low-power two-wheeler market, dominated by TVS Suzuki Ltd and Majestic Auto.
Kinetic showed net profits of 134.8 million rupees in 1996/97 (April-March), 2.7 percent down from 138.5 million rupees the previous year.
